title: Presentability and monoidal structure of model localizations
statement: Use [def-coef-complete-algebroid] for infinity-category, universe, and smallness conventions. Let $\mathcal M$ be a combinatorial model category: it is locally presentable, complete and cocomplete, with weak equivalences $W$, cofibrations $C$ and fibrations $F$, where $W$ is retract-closed and satisfies two-out-of-three, and $(C,F\cap W)$ and $(C\cap W,F)$ are weak factorization systems generated by sets and admitting functorial factorizations. Locally presentable means cocomplete and generated under the filtered colimits for some regular cardinal by a small set of objects whose ordinary Hom functors preserve those colimits. A weak factorization system is a pair of mutually characterized left/right diagonal-lifting classes with factorization of every arrow. The homotopy coherent localization of $\mathcal M$ means an infinity category receiving the nerve $N(\mathcal M)$ such that restriction identifies its functor infinity category into any infinity category with the full subcategory of functors from $N(\mathcal M)$ carrying $W$ to equivalences. Then the homotopy coherent localization $\mathcal M[W^{-1}]_\infty$ is a presentable infinity category. If $\mathcal M$ is closed symmetric monoidal, its unit is cofibrant, and the pushout product of two cofibrations is a cofibration, trivial when either factor is trivial, then this localization has a symmetric monoidal structure computed by tensoring cofibrant replacements. Its tensor preserves small colimits separately. Here trivial means belonging to $W$, cofibrant means its initial map is a cofibration, and pushout product of $A\to B$ and $A'\to B'$ means $(B\otimes A')\amalg_{A\otimes A'}(A\otimes B')\to B\otimes B'$. The localization retains mapping spaces and their coherent compositions, rather than only the ordinary homotopy category.

source.place: Proposition 1.3.4.22, Corollary 1.3.4.26 and section 4.1.7, especially Proposition 4.1.7.4 and Example 4.1.7.6 Read online where available; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical result.

proof.text:
Write $\mathcal M^c$ for the full subcategory of cofibrant objects and choose a functorial cofibrant replacement $e:Q\to\mathrm{id}$. If $w:X\to Y$ is a weak equivalence, $e_YQw=we_X$ and two-out-of-three show that $Qw$ is a weak equivalence. Thus both inclusion and $Q$ induce functors on homotopy coherent localizations. Their two composites are equivalent to the identities by the components of $e$, restricted to $\mathcal M^c$ for the other composite. The localization universal property includes natural transformations, so these are coherent equivalences. Hence
$$N(\mathcal M^c)[W_c^{-1}]_\infty\simeq N(\mathcal M)[W^{-1}]_\infty.$$
This also applies to the other model categories below.

source.place: Remark 1.3.4.16; functorial replacement argument written out

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-combinatorial-presheaf-presentation] to $\mathcal M$. Obtain a small $D$, a small set $S$ of arrows, $\mathcal B=L_S\mathsf U(D)$, and a Quillen equivalence $L:\mathcal B\rightleftarrows\mathcal M:R$. Both $\mathcal B$ and $\mathcal M$ have functorial replacements. No simplicial structure or properness of $\mathcal M$ is required by this presentation theorem.

By [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction], the Quillen pair gives $\mathbf LL\dashv\mathbf RR$ on homotopy coherent localizations, with its stated replacement formulas for the unit and counit. These are equivalences: for cofibrant $A\in\mathcal B$, the fibrant replacement $LA\to TLA$ is a weak equivalence, so the Quillen-equivalence criterion in [lem-coef-combinatorial-presheaf-presentation] makes its adjunct $A\to RTLA$ a weak equivalence. For fibrant $Y\in\mathcal M$, the weak equivalence $QRY\to RY$ has cofibrant source; the same criterion makes its adjunct $LQRY\to Y$ a weak equivalence. These arrows represent the derived unit and counit. Every object has a cofibrant or fibrant replacement, so their components are equivalences everywhere. Thus $\mathcal B_\infty\simeq\mathcal M_\infty$.

source.place: Lemma 1.3.4.21, with the actual derived unit and counit

proof.text: Put $\mathcal P=\operatorname{Fun}(N(D)^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S)$, which is presentable by [lem-coef-space-presheaf-presentability]. The first comparison of [lem-coef-simplicial-presheaf-localization-comparison] sends the small set $S$ to a small set $\overline S$ of arrows of $\mathcal P$. Apply the small-set clause of [lem-coef-presentable-infinity-adjoints] to $\overline S$: the full subcategory $\mathcal P_{\overline S\text{-loc}}$ is presentable. The second comparison of [lem-coef-simplicial-presheaf-localization-comparison] identifies it with $\mathcal B_\infty$. Step 3 identifies that with $\mathcal M_\infty$. Existence of colimits and generation by a small collection of sufficiently presentable objects are preserved by an equivalence, since it identifies mapping spaces and their universal properties. This proves presentability of the localization in the statement.

source.place: Proof of Proposition A.3.7.6, localized-presheaf case; Remark 5.5.3.7 and Proposition 5.5.4.15

proof.text: Now assume the stated closed symmetric monoidal hypotheses. For cofibrant $K$, closedness makes $K\otimes-$ and $-\otimes K$ left adjoints; in particular they send the initial object to an initial object. The pushout product $(0\to K)\mathbin{\square}(A\to B)$ is consequently $K\otimes A\to K\otimes B$, a cofibration and a trivial cofibration when $A\to B$ is trivial. Thus both partial tensor functors are left Quillen. With $0\to A$ and $0\to B$, the pushout-product axiom gives the cofibrancy of $A\otimes B$. The unit is cofibrant by hypothesis. Therefore the ordinary symmetric monoidal structure restricts to $\mathcal M^c$.

source.place: Example 4.1.7.6; pushout-product calculation and closed adjunctions written out

proof.text: The preservation clause of [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction] applied to the two partial left Quillen functors of Step 5 shows that tensor by any cofibrant $K$ carries weak equivalences between cofibrant objects to weak equivalences. Thus $W_c$ is stable under both tensor variables in $\mathcal M^c$. It contains all isomorphisms and is closed under composition. In the ordinary nerve it is automatically stable under homotopy, since homotopic parallel edges there are equal. These are the precise tensor-stability hypotheses needed for monoidal localization.

source.place: Example 4.1.7.6; weak-equivalence preservation is the Brown clause of the cited derived-adjunction theorem

proof.text:
Apply [lem-coef-relative-symmetric-monoidal-localization] to the symmetric monoidal nerve of $\mathcal M^c$ and the system $W_c$. It yields a symmetric monoidal structure on $N(\mathcal M^c)[W_c^{-1}]_\infty$ with the localization functor strong symmetric monoidal. Use the equivalence of Step 1 as a model of $\mathcal M_\infty$. Its tensor on represented objects is therefore
$$qX\otimes^{\mathbf L}qY\simeq q(QX\otimes QY),\qquad \mathbf1\simeq q(\mathbf1_{\mathcal M}).$$
All constraints and their higher coherences come from the cited theorem. The arrows $QQ'X\to QX$ and $QQ'X\to Q'X$ induced by two replacement transformations are weak equivalences between cofibrant objects; Step 6 makes their tensors with cofibrant objects weak equivalences. Consequently the formula is independent of replacement through these natural equivalences.

Fix a cofibrant $K$. The closed adjunction $K\otimes-\dashv\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(K,-)$ is Quillen by Step 5. By [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction] it induces a genuine mapping-space adjunction on $\mathcal M_\infty$ whose left adjoint sends $qX$ to $q(K\otimes QX)$. This is the tensor-by-$qK$ functor of Step 7, because $QK\to K$ is a weak equivalence between cofibrant objects and Step 6 applies. Since $\mathcal M_\infty$ is presentable by Step 4, the adjoint criterion of [lem-coef-presentable-infinity-adjoints] shows that this functor preserves every small colimit. The identical argument for $-\otimes K$, or symmetry, proves preservation in the other variable. Every object is represented up to equivalence by a cofibrant $K$, so this proves separate cocontinuity for all objects, including the empty colimit. All adjunctions and comparisons used are at the mapping-space level.

source.place: Corollary 1.3.4.26; alternatively the derived mapping-space adjunction and HTT Corollary 5.5.2.9
